chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yusuf ibn Aqil, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) issued a ruling regarding a female slave whom her master had intercourse with during the period of purity (before menstruation), then sold her to another man before she menstruated. The second man had intercourse with her, and she had not yet menstruated. Then both men had intercourse with her during the same period of purity. She gave birth to a boy, and they disputed over him. The mother of the boy was asked, and she claimed that both men had intercourse with her during the same period of purity, so she did not know which of them was the father. He (peace be upon him) ruled: 'Regarding the boy, he inherits from both of them, and they inherit from him equally.'

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: We have clarified in the Book of Marriage in this book that if two men have intercourse with a girl after the transfer of ownership from one to the other, the child is linked to the one in whose possession the girl is at the time. We cited reports on this. And if they both had intercourse with her during the same period of purity while they were partners without transfer of ownership from one to the other, lots are cast between them, and the child is linked to the one whose name is drawn. There is no reason to repeat this narration here. The explanation for this report is that it was presented as an act of precautionary dissimulation (taqiyyah), because it agrees with the views of some of the Sunni scholars, just as other reports have been presented in this manner.

key_terms.قُبُلِ طُهْرِهَا: Beginning of the period of purity (before menstruation)
key_terms.يَرِثُهُمَا كِلَيْهِمَا: He inherits from both of them

ai.seo_question: How is paternity determined and inheritance distributed when a female slave has intercourse with two owners during the same period of purity?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* illustrates a specific legal scenario where a female slave was sold and had intercourse with both the former and new master during the same period of purity, resulting in a child with uncertain paternity. Imam al-Sadiq ruled that the child inherits from both men equally, a decision the commentator attributes to *taqiyya* to align with certain Sunni views, contrasting with the standard Shia rule of casting lots for simultaneous intercourse. This highlights the nuanced application of *iddah* (waiting period) and *shibh al-iddah* in determining paternity when menstruation has not yet occurred to confirm the end of the period.
